sn36.11:2.1: The Buddha praises the mendicant because he had the critical acumen to notice these apparently different explanations, and, rather than assuming they were contradictory, or just ignoring the problem, he asked the Buddha for clarification.
sn36.11:2.15: The “progressive cessation of conditions” (_anupubbasaṅkhārānaṁ nirodho_) is also found at [sn36.15]() and [sn36.17](). It is similar to the nine “progressive cessations” of [an9.31]() and [dn33:3.2.82](), except it goes even further to full enlightenment, as in the “progressive cessation in a definitive sense” at [an9.61]().
sn36.11:2.31: This is the only time these are mentioned.
